question: Hypothyroidism is caused by which of the following anti-tubercular drug -
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ethionamide" -> "inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis" -> "reduced thyroid hormone levels" -> "hypothyroidism" -> 85%
CHAIN: "PAS" -> "possible interference with thyroid function" -> "unclear impact on thyroid hormone levels" -> "possible hypothyroidism" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Cycloserine" -> "no known effect on thyroid function" -> "unlikely to cause hypothyroidism" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Pyrazinamide" -> "no known effect on thyroid function" -> "unlikely to cause hypothyroidism" -> 20%
analysis: The question asks which anti-tubercular drug is known to cause hypothyroidism. Among the options provided, ethionamide is recognized in medical literature as having the potential to inhibit thyroid hormone synthesis, which can lead to hypothyroidism. This aligns with the consensus that ethionamide can cause hypothyroidism as a side effect. PAS, while having some unclear impact on thyroid function, does not have a strong consensus linking it directly to hypothyroidism. Cycloserine and Pyrazinamide have no known effects on thyroid function and are unlikely to cause hypothyroidism. Therefore, based on the available evidence and medical consensus, ethionamide is the most likely drug to cause hypothyroidism.
